title: CI rule: every exercise has tests + solutionVerified:true + starter-fails; block publish otherwise
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). The correctness gate is the most important quality mechanism, but it only works if CI enforces it for every exercise — not just the ones the author remembered to verify. A CI rule that blocks publication of any exercise lacking tests, a reference solution, solutionVerified:true, or a failing starter is the automation backstop that prevents the dominant failure mode (a broken/unsolvable exercise) from reaching learners.
objective: Add a CI rule that fails the build for any exercise that lacks a test suite, lacks a reference solution, has solutionVerified:false (or unset), or whose starter code already passes the tests — blocking publication until all four conditions are met.
acceptanceCriteria: CI fails if any exercise is missing a test suite.
CI fails if any exercise is missing a referenceSolution.
CI fails if any exercise has solutionVerified:false or solutionVerified not set.
CI fails if the starter code already passes the exercise's tests (starter-must-fail check).
All four checks run on every PR and push to main; failure messages identify the offending exercise.
The rule applies to all languages (Python and JavaScript at minimum).
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
A test case demonstrates each failure mode triggers the CI block.
output: A merged PR adding the four-part CI exercise-completeness and correctness rule, with test cases for each failure mode.
